title: 1966 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Let \(s_1\) be the sum of the first \(n\) terms of the arithmetic sequence \(8,\) \(12,\) \(\ldots\) and let \(s_2\) be the sum of the first \(n\) terms of the arithmetic sequence \(17,\) \(19,\) \(\ldots.\) Then \(s_1=s_2\) for:

solutions.text:
The two sums are \[ \begin{gathered} s_1=2n^2+6n,\\ s_2=n^2+16n. \end{gathered} \] Equality gives \(n(n-10)=0.\) Since a number of terms is positive, only \(n=10\) works, so there is one value.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Write a sum formula for each progression
Cancel the positive factor \(n\) after equating the sums
